The Borrowed Jacket

A shared apartment, a blue jacket on the sofa, and everyday items in the wrong place. Who is the real owner?

01 · Warm-Up

After the Party

Look at the living room after a get-together. Tap your reaction, then answer in 1 minute.

1. Setup: Show the After the Party photo and 3 speech bubbles (3–4 min). Students tap "Every weekend!" or "Not in my house!" (no percentages or scores).
2. Modeling: Model with [P] ONLY (To Be + possessive adjectives my, your): "Is your room tidy or messy after a party? — My room is messy!" Do NOT introduce 's or Whose yet.
3. Check: Run a 1-minute oral reaction using [P]. Enforce boundary [F]: NO have/has, NO mine/yours, and NO action verbs (borrow, take, use, wear).
4. Keys: Open-ended personal responses with My room is tidy / messy!
Sofa "A blue jacket on the sofa!"
Floor "A white charger on the floor!"
Door "Glasses near the door!"
Your 1-Tap Reaction

1-Minute Reaction

02 · Vocabulary

6 Everyday Personal Items

Listen to each word and example. Click a card to see the meaning.

1. Setup: Have students play the Word and Example audio on all 6 cards before flipping to read the meanings.
2. Modeling: Practice the 6 items using ONLY [P] (My jacket is blue. / His charger is white. / Her keys are on the table.). Then drill the Pronunciation Focus: final -s /s/ (jackets) vs. /z/ (keys, glasses).
3. Check: Students complete Room Zone Bin Sort by tapping each chip and sorting it into Zone A: On Me or Zone B: In Bag / On Desk, then click Check Zones.
4. Keys: Zone A: On Me = jacket, glasses, watch · Zone B: In Bag / On Desk = charger, keys, bag.

Pronunciation Focus

Final -s: /s/ vs. /z/

Listen to the final sound on plural objects: soft /s/ in jackets vs. voiced buzz /z/ in keys and glasses.

jackets /ˈdʒæk.ɪts/ → /s/ Soft air sound, no throat buzz: Two jackets.
keys /kiːz/ · glasses /ˈɡlæs.ɪz/ → /z/ Voice buzzes at the end: My keys and my glasses.

03 · USA Chunks

3 Useful USA Phrases

Use these 3 phrases as one piece in a shared room or apartment.

1. Setup: Present these 3 expressions as ready-to-use conversational blocks [L].
2. Modeling: Play each Phrase and Example audio. Do NOT analyze grammar inside "Who left this here?" (past verb left is taught only as part of this fixed block).
3. Check: Quick choral repetition + mini-reaction: Teacher points to a charger on the desk and asks "Who left this here?" → Students react with "Hands off!" or "Finders keepers!".
4. Keys: All 3 chunks appear in the Housemates' Notes reading next.
"Hands off!" Boundary
/hændz ɔːf/
Hey! That's my jacket—hands off!
Flip ↻
Meaning
"Hands off!"

Do not touch this! It is not your item.

Use together Flip ↺

/huː lɛft ðɪs hɪr/
A charger on the sofa—who left this here?
Flip ↻

"Who left this here?"

/ˈfaɪn.dərz ˈkiː.pərz/

"Finders keepers!"

04 · Reading

Housemates' Notes

Read the 3 notes from Sofia, Mateo, and Diego. Then answer the 3 questions.

1. Setup: Ask students to read the 3 notes silently (4 min) and spot all 3 USA Chunks before answering the comprehension questions. Play the optional Reading audio (Listen (after reading)) only after silent reading.
2. Modeling: Point out Whose jacket is this?, Whose keys are these?, and the 's names (Mateo's jacket, Sofia's glasses, Diego's jacket) as an inductive preview for Grammar.
3. Check: Students answer the 3 Comprehension Check questions (written in [P]) individually, then justify each answer with a line from the notes.
4. Keys: 1. B (No, it isn't — it's blue.) · 2. A (Yes, they are — they're Sofia's glasses.) · 3. C (It's on the table.).
Note 01 · Sofa & Desk
Sofia
26 · Room A

"Hey everyone! Whose jacket is this? It's blue, and it's on the sofa. Who left this here? It isn't my jacket. Is it Mateo's jacket? Maybe it's Diego's jacket. Hands off my charger on the desk, please!"

Note 02 · Table Items
Mateo
29 · Room B

"Hi! That blue jacket isn't my jacket—my jacket is black. Are these Sofia's glasses on the table? Yes, they're Sofia's glasses! And whose keys are these? They're silver. Finders keepers! No, no!"

Note 03 · Near the Door
Diego
24 · Room C

"Good morning! That blue jacket is my jacket—it's Diego's jacket! Sorry! And whose bag is this near the door? It's Mateo's bag! Mateo's watch is on the table too. Who left this here? Our shared apartment is busy today!"

Check Your Reading

1. Is the jacket on the sofa black?
2. Are the glasses on the table for Sofia?
3. Where is the watch from Note 03?
05 · Grammar

Saxon Genitive ('s) & Whose

Ask who owns an item and name the owner clearly.

1. Setup: Connect back to Housemates' Notes ("Whose jacket is this?", "It's Diego's jacket.", "Are these Sofia's glasses?").
2. Modeling: Highlight Name + 's + item (Ana's jacket, NOT *the jacket of Ana*) and the singular/plural question contrast: Whose is this? vs. Whose are these? Enforce [F]: NO mine/yours, NO double genitive (a friend of mine's), NO have/has.
3. Check: Students complete Lost & Found Tagging on the 4 item cards (selecting question, pronoun, and 's form) and click Tag Item.
4. Keys: 1. Whose is this? / It's Diego's jacket. · 2. Whose is this? / It's Mateo's charger. · 3. Whose are these? / They're Sofia's keys. · 4. Whose are these? / They're Ana's glasses.

Add 's after a person's name to show the owner (Ana's jacket). Use Whose is this? for one item and Whose are these? for two or more items.

Form Structure Singular (1 Item) Plural (2+ Items)
Affirmative Name + 's + item It's Ana's jacket. They're Mateo's keys.
Negative isn't / aren't + Name + 's + item It isn't Sofia's bag. They aren't Diego's glasses.
Yes/No Question Is this / Are these + Name + 's + item? Is this Mateo's charger? Are these Ana's keys?
Wh- Question Whose (+ item) + is this / are these? Whose is this? / Whose watch is this? Whose are these? / Whose keys are these?

06 · Speaking

Mystery Bag (Tap to Pull)

Pull 1 lost item from the bag. You have 30 seconds to ask, claim, or joke with your roommate—no script!

1. Setup: Pair students as roommates (in 1-on-1, you play the second roommate). Tap Pull 1 Item to reveal one random object + suspect and start the 30-second live timer.
2. Modeling: Demo 1 item in 15 seconds using Whose is this? / Whose are these?, 's, and a USA Chunk ("Hands off!", "Who left this here?", "Finders keepers!"). Keep the screen free of written sentences.
3. Check: Monitor without interrupting and verify the 4 items in Speaking Checklist (What Counts). Note any *the jacket of Diego*, *It's mine*, or *Who have...?* slips for delayed feedback.
4. Keys: 6 items in bag: Blue Jacket (Diego?), White Charger (Sofia?), Silver Keys (Mateo?), Black Bag (Ana?), Brown Glasses (Sofia?), Silver Watch (Mateo?).

07 · Exit Ticket

Whose Is This?

Write 1 Whose question and 2 sentences with 's about items in your room or bag.

1. Setup: Give 3–4 minutes for independent writing in the blank textarea without copying a model.
2. Modeling: Remind students to include: (1) 1 Whose question (singular or plural), and (2) 2 sentences with 's (e.g., Ana's keys, Mateo's bag).
3. Check: Students click Check My Note, read aloud, and self-verify the 3 Can-Do statements.
4. Keys: Understanding Comes Before Advancement: advance to A1.1-U02-L03 only when the student achieves E2 (accurate Whose + 's without have/has, mine/yours, or action verbs).
